answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks whose results are independently checked and backed by a stake that is forfeited when a claim is disproved. A newcomer may create a haven of identities, but each one must lock scarce funds and build a separate record of verified work; splitting a stake across accounts does not multiply voting weight. An attacker therefore pays capital and time for every credible persona, while coordinated fake work risks slashing the whole stake. A cedar or dune-themed profile gains no privilege merely by appearing distinct.
